packs.title: Lines Above the Pacific
packs.promise: Find a small Lima story between the coast and the next curious detail.

q.s: Collect three different edges above the Pacific.
st: Choose a roomy stopping place on the public pedestrian path in Parque Antonio Raimondi. Face the sea from behind the protective boundary.
Find three different kinds of edge: one nearly straight, one curved and one broken into repeated pieces. Look among the horizon, paths, planting borders, railings and distant coastline.
Give each edge a verb: stretches, bends, skips, or a word of your own. Describe what makes your three edges different.
Save the three edges and their verbs as a small portrait of this stretch of coast.

q.s: Give a wide view a very small caption.
st: Choose a comfortable public place to pause in Parque Salazar, clear of entrances and the pedestrian flow.
Choose one nearby detail and one distant detail. A path seam and a band of sea, a leaf and a cloud, or two visible features in the mist will work.
Write exactly six words that connect the two details. Try one version, then change a word to make it sound more like your own voice.
Save your final six words with the two details that inspired them.

q.s: Find the rhythm on either side of a library entrance.
st: From the public park, face the library façade without standing in its entrance or on its steps.
Imagine a vertical line through the central entrance. Find two pairs of details that answer each other on the left and right, such as window shapes, columns or decorative edges.
Find one detail on the centre line that gives the building a focal point. Describe how it differs from your paired details.
Save a tiny three-part inventory: left and right pair one, left and right pair two, and the centre detail.

packs.title: Portals, Towers and Small Stories
packs.promise: Read carved entrances, collect street rhythms and make a small story of your own.

q.s: Collect three kinds of line from one carved entrance.
st: From public space, face San Francisco’s dark carved central portal between its yellow bell-tower bases, or use the Ministry of Culture’s portal photograph.
Find one curve, one upright line and one curling or branching carved edge. Study visible forms without touching the stone.
Draw three separate strokes or describe where each line turns. Give each a short original verb and keep the three together.

q.s: Send an ordinary object on a four-panel imagined journey.
st: Study the former station’s three arched openings, vertical façade details and roof clock from public space, or use the Ministry of Culture exterior photograph.
Choose an ordinary object of your own, such as a paper ticket or pencil. Give it an imagined arrival, a wait, a change of plan and a departure.
Draw four small panels or write four short lines. Include one visible façade shape in each and save your original journey.

q.s: Collect repetitions across a restored street front.
st: Face Osambela’s blue exterior from a roomy permitted sidewalk position, or use the Congress exterior photograph.
Find a repetition in the enclosed wooden balconies, another in window outlines and a third in visible ironwork. Count only what your viewpoint shows.
Record each rhythm with a short sequence of marks or a written description. Keep your three sequences as a small façade inventory.
